name: Kundler Klamm
kurzbeschreibung: Kundler Klamm enchants as an accessible natural gorge between Kundl and Wildschönau featuring rushing waters, soaring cliffs, and Tyrolean marble.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Kundler Klamm gorge is acclaimed as one of the most scenic and easily walkable natural canyons in Austria. Carving a stunning passageway between the idyllic high valley of Wildschönau and the market town of Kundl in the lower Tyrolean Inn Valley, the gorge was sculpted over millions of years by the fierce waters of the Wildschönauer Ache river. Hemmed in by towering rock faces reaching heights of over two hundred vertical meters, crystalline mountain currents surge over thundering cascades and through swirling natural rock basins. This pristine natural sanctuary delights hikers, geology lovers, and families looking for accessible alpine tranquility.

Route & Requirements

The walking trail through the gorge is distinguished by its exceptional width, gentle grading, and absence of steep inclines. Stretching approximately 3.5 kilometers one way, the well-maintained gravel path follows the rushing mountain torrent and is ideally suited for families with strollers and seniors alike. Dramatic rock overhangs, shaded resting benches, and sturdy wooden footbridges line the enjoyable route. Geologically, the canyon is celebrated for deposits of colorful Kundler marble and ancient fossil sediments; children delight in scouring the shallow gravel banks for smooth decorative stones. Following historical rockfalls, the pathway has been heavily fortified with modern rockfall netting and covered galleries. Casual leisure footwear is perfectly sufficient.

Visit & Arrival

The gorge is open annually from early May through October 31 during daylight hours. Admission to the natural monument is completely free. For safety reasons due to ice and seasonal rockfall risks, the canyon remains strictly closed throughout winter. Arrival by car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kramsach or Wörgl West) to Kundl; paid parking is available right at the northern entrance. By public transit: ÖBB train to Kundl station, followed by a signposted 25-minute walk to the gorge entrance. Alternatively, take the whimsical Wildschönau vintage slow train (Bummelzug) from Mühltal directly to the southern gorge gateway.

Tips

Stop by the historic Sandbichler stone-turning workshop at the northern entrance, the only craft workshop in Tyrol transforming raw river stones into polished ornamental spheres and jewelry. After your scenic hike, the traditional Gasthaus Kundler Klamm inn welcomes guests to delicious Tyrolean dishes and cold drinks in its shaded beer garden. Remember to bring a light jacket, as the deep gorge maintains pleasant coolness even on hot summer afternoons.
preis: Free admission (Wildschönau slow train fee applies separately)
oeffnungszeiten: Early May to late October during daylight hours (closed in winter for safety)
